_provenance: AUTHORED source of truth for the book's metaphors AND slogans — the writing techniques that elaborate a declared idea — so the house rules 'one slogan per idea / ration polished slogans / never open a 2nd image before the 1st pays off' are MEASURABLE. Every entry carries a `kind` discriminator (metaphor | slogan) and an `elaborates: {model, id}` link to the declared idea it expands (the join that makes 'one idea, several competing slogans' detectable). Metaphor entries live in `metaphors`, slogans in `slogans`; both share name/slug/notes and diverge on the fields their governing rule needs. book-models/metaphor_spans_model.py projects the inventory + structural + overlap + density checks; metaphor_slogan_index_model.py derives every occurrence from the built HTML. Edit an entry HERE. Anchors are heading/index-def/point slugs (stable across prose edits), NOT line numbers; re-resolve an anchor with `python3 book-models/metaphor_spans_model.py anchors`.
overlap_rule: A LOCAL metaphor must pay off before the next LOCAL metaphor is introduced within the same stretch. CORE vocabulary (the Printer, churn, map-and-territory, the Model Zoo, the loop, the engineer's seat) is always live and exempt. Overlap = two locals in one stretch whose [introduced_at, pays_off_at] spans intersect. Any real overlap must be ratified (overlap_ok:true + a rationale on either party) or it is a finding.
ration_rule: Each declared idea gets ONE canonical slogan (scope invoke-by-name) at its best location. Later appearances are blunt referential invocations, not fresh polished formulations. A `used-once` line appears exactly once; a `commandment` may recur as a refrain. Density/clustering caps ration polished occurrences. A slogan and a metaphor elaborating the SAME idea do not compete — only two invoke-by-name slogans on one idea do.

metaphors.name: The Printer
metaphors.vehicle: a 3D printer, not a coder or a stapler
metaphors.payoff: A bad build indicts the instructions, not the machine.
metaphors.notes: The governing metaphor. Boundary named in 1.3 (loops-and-models); revisited at the close in 6.3-conclusion. Sub-images (stapler, CAD/slicing, the open-ended-technology siblings) belong to this cluster, not separate rows.

metaphors.name: Churn
metaphors.payoff: The wall a fleet hits; the governed environment pushes it back.
metaphors.notes: Named as recurring vocabulary on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Cashed as an empirical curve in 5.2-the-timeline-and-the-work (anchor churn): peaks at mechanization, then collapses.

metaphors.name: Engineering capital
metaphors.vehicle: financial capital that earns compounding interest, not error that snowballs
metaphors.payoff: The stock the positive dual of churn accrues; it earns returns while it stays fit, and depreciates when it does not.
metaphors.notes: The vehicle for the compounding principle — attached to the STOCK (engineering capital), so flow (compounding) and stock stay coherent. Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core); pays off in Part 6 (the Compounding-Governance proposition + the Bureaucracy-vs-Engineering-capital section, where technical debt is set against engineering capital). Compound INTEREST, deliberately: it fixes the valence against the pre-existing opposite-sign term `compounding-failure-probability` (Part 4). No vehicle collision — no prior `capital`/`compound` span exists.

metaphors.name: Map and territory
metaphors.vehicle: a map drops detail and is not the land
metaphors.payoff: Justifies the drift and parity gates that keep map equal to territory.
metaphors.notes: Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Does real work in 2.2-models-and-the-semantic-gap (anchor map-and-territory): model is the map, code the territory, hand-sync drifts. Elaborates the DEFINITION of `model` — the map that drops detail IS the model of the code.

metaphors.name: The Model Zoo
metaphors.vehicle: a zoo of executable models on tour
metaphors.payoff: The 4+1 views, each walked as a drift-gated model over real code.
metaphors.notes: Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Opens and carries all of Part 3, from 3.1-the-executable-zoo (anchor model-zoo) onward.

metaphors.name: The loop
metaphors.payoff: Agent work is a loop you engineer at four control points.
metaphors.notes: "Nearly everything in this book is an instance of it." The four levers land in 1.3; recurs book-wide. Elaborates the DEFINITION of the engineered agent loop.

metaphors.name: The engineer's seat
metaphors.vehicle: two seats — the engineer's and the developer's
metaphors.payoff: The developer's seat moves to the fleet; humans keep the engineering seats.
metaphors.notes: Classed core (medium confidence): anchors chapter 1.5 and is cashed in the back matter (6.2-implications-for-se). If read as a chapter-local frame, reclassify local — it is then the sole local in 1.5 (still no overlap).

metaphors.name: The reasoning horizon
metaphors.vehicle: a horizon bounding how much reasoning state a task can hold at once
metaphors.payoff: Models extend the horizon; MAGE moves the wall, it does not remove it.
metaphors.notes: Core vocabulary from 1.1 onward: the reasoning-horizon reframe of the Modeling Thesis recurs across the preface, 1.4, 2.3, 3.1/3.7, and the theory chapter's Reasoning-Horizon Proposition (6.0). Sub-images 'reasoning state' and 'working memory' belong to this cluster, not separate rows. Spatial vehicle named once, then used plainly (the define-once discipline). Elaborates the DEFINITION of `reasoning-horizon`.

metaphors.name: Poka-yoke / the fixture
metaphors.vehicle: a jig that will not seat a bad part
metaphors.payoff: Mistake-proofing: shape the work so the defect cannot happen.
metaphors.notes: Pays off in place, in the paragraph that raises it.

metaphors.name: The raven and the pebbles
metaphors.vehicle: Aesop's raven raising water to reach it
metaphors.payoff: A goal-directed agent takes indirect steps toward a target.
metaphors.notes: Local (kept, NOT retired). The raven vignette was cut from the §2.1 web body (Part-2 revision); its payoff now lives in the agent DEFINITION aspect (definitions.json -> agent -> aspects[0], 'a raven dropping pebbles to raise the water it cannot otherwise reach') — def-model/PDF-homed and web-absent, not the chapter body. The image still teaches the agent definition via the def-box aspect and the PDF, so it stays a live local metaphor (no count change; local stays local). Elaborates definitions/agent; re-anchored to the recast opener point `controllable-not-controlled-is-why-authority-leaves-the-prompt`, which now carries the agent index-def after the R11 def-apparatus excision (M3 clean).

metaphors.name: The evidence staircase
metaphors.payoff: Cheap checks early bind an exact tree; later stages check the binding instead of trusting a self-report.
metaphors.notes: Vehicle word 'staircase' is reused by mage-staircase (5.4) — see the vehicle-collision check. Renaming this to 'the evidence ladder/ratchet' (a DEFERRED editorial call, no content edit here) would free 'staircase' for the load-bearing 5.4 close.

metaphors.name: The coin
metaphors.payoff: Fuzzing and property testing draw one oracle from one spec.
metaphors.notes: Carried by the figure 'The Coin Is the Model' in the same section.

metaphors.name: The DOJ ramp
metaphors.vehicle: call-ahead-for-a-ramp versus the ramp is simply there
metaphors.payoff: Accessibility as a property present by default, not requested on demand.
metaphors.notes: The DOJ's own analogy, carried in the burden-shift table. The ramp present-by-default is reliability from the environment, not on demand.

metaphors.name: The MAGE staircase
metaphors.vehicle: a five-rung climb of delegated jobs
metaphors.payoff: Each rung fixes what broke the rung below; the climb ends at MAGE.
metaphors.notes: The book's structural climb; shares the vehicle word 'staircase' with evidence-staircase (2.3), a different Part.

metaphors.name: The scar healed into a wall
metaphors.vehicle: a scar that heals into a load-bearing wall
metaphors.payoff: A failure, once converted, hardens into permanent structure.
metaphors.notes: NEW (part1.md). Used-once vivid image: 'Use scar once.' A converted failure heals into load-bearing structure. Anchor empty until the net-subtractive fix-wave marks the paragraph; density lint's used-once class guards the single occurrence.

metaphors.name: The model bridge
metaphors.vehicle: a bridge the agents reason across
metaphors.payoff: The governed channel the agents reason across between code and authored models — traceability edges plus drift checks, kept as one derived source, not a drifting snapshot.
metaphors.notes: CORE (reclassified from local, 260806): the teaching handle for the models-bridge concept — model-code traceability + drift-checking, the governed channel between the code (territory) and the authored models (map). Elaborates definitions/models-bridge (the concept's formal def), the same concept-term target the core map-and-territory metaphor uses for definitions/model. Core by CROSS-PART PAYOFF SPAN (2.2 -> 3.8 -> 4.4 -> 6.2), not by 0.3-glossary registration — the engineers-seat 'medium confidence' core basis, an always-live cross-Part vocabulary: SEEDED at 2.2 (structured-model-layer figure, without the literal words), DEFINED at 3.8 (book_home + index-def), PAID OFF at 4.4 (the governed path from authored models into the agent's task context and checks). No pays_off_at (core never ends) and no stretch (overlap-exempt). ssot-not-snapshot is now ADJACENT — a property of the bridge (kept-derived), carried by its own slogan derived-defends-snapshotted-drifts, no longer co-elaborated by this metaphor. Distinct image from reasoning-horizon; vehicle word 'model' echoes model-zoo across a different stretch (accepted audit-only vehicle-collision).

slogans.name: Printer posture
slogans.canonical: Treat the agent as a printer, not a coder.
competitors: builds exactly what its instructions describe
can execute from a structured model, not a vibe
slogans.notes: Later uses: 'The printer posture applies here', not a new polished line.

slogans.name: Failure diagnosis
slogans.canonical: Read a bad build first as evidence about the instructions.
competitors: suspect the instructions before the agent
slogans.notes: The printer-cluster diagnosis slogan; elaborates a DIFFERENT claim than printer-posture (fault-lies-in-instructions vs printer-not-coder), so they do not compete.

slogans.name: Governance conversion
slogans.canonical: Convert recurring failure into a durable mechanism.
competitors: spend attention once per failure class
slogans.notes: The governance move stated once, then invoked by name.

slogans.name: Review replacement
competitors: reliability from the environment, not repeated inspection
slogans.notes: Points at the apparatus-is-the-review claim added to claims_declared.json (ratified decision A) — a major book claim that previously had no declared home.

slogans.name: Reasoning limit
competitors: too much to hold in mind at once
slogans.notes: Compresses the reasoning-horizon DEFINITION (ratified decision B: definitions is a fifth allowed elaborates namespace).

slogans.name: Danger in the instructions
slogans.canonical: The danger was already in the instructions; the speed just gets you there first.
slogans.notes: A used-once vivid line — appears exactly once. Co-elaborates fault-lies-in-instructions beside the failure-diagnosis canonical (a sanctioned co-elaboration, not a second canonical).

slogans.name: One trunk, five views
slogans.notes: NEW (Part-3 revision). The Model-Zoo / 4+1 framing: one core architecture projected as five views. Elaborates the Modeling-Thesis Big-Idea (the model-zoo metaphor's namespace); no other invoke-by-name slogan lands on modeling-thesis, so no competing-canonical. Anchor empty until the Part-3 fix-wave marks the canonical landing.

slogans.name: Derived defends, snapshotted drifts
competitors: a check that re-reads the code can't fall behind it; a stored copy can
slogans.notes: NEW (Part-3 revision). A derived check re-reads the code and cannot fall behind it; a hand-updated snapshot is a second source that drifts. Sole elaborator of ssot-not-snapshot; the model-bridge core metaphor now elaborates the broader models-bridge concept (definitions/models-bridge), of which kept-derived is one property (a metaphor + a slogan do not compete — only two invoke-by-name slogans on one idea do). Anchor empty until the Part-3 fix-wave marks the canonical landing.

slogans.name: Profile edit, not graph edit
slogans.notes: NEW (Part-3 revision). The Physical View: host-specific resource limits are a per-host scheduler profile over one shared invariant-DAG, not a forked execution graph per host. Elaborates the profile-edit-not-graph-edit claim added to claims_declared.json (it was a REAL dangler — no declared claim carried the idea; same pattern as apparatus-is-the-review). Anchor empty until the Part-3 fix-wave marks the canonical landing.
